It is an easy place for breakfast, brunch or a break with your dog in Algés, whatever the weather.

286.description: Fresco Lisboa, on Rua Tomás da Anunciação in Campo de Ourique, welcomes dogs of any size indoors and on its terrace. The restaurant specialises in healthy, light meals, including bowls, wraps, açaí, breakfast and brunch dishes, juices and smoothies. With a choice of indoor and outdoor seating, it is a convenient place to eat with your dog in Lisbon.

287.description: Don Pablo, on Rua Silva Carvalho in Campo de Ourique, Lisbon, welcomes dogs of any size indoors and on its terrace, with no additional restrictions specified. Its Portuguese-inspired menu focuses on sharing plates, including croquettes, broken eggs, alheira, fish, meat and vegetarian dishes. It is a friendly option for lunch or dinner with your dog in Campo de Ourique.

288.description: Parque e Palácio de Monserrate in Sintra includes historic gardens where dogs are welcome. Dogs enter free of charge, but owners must obtain a dog ticket on arrival. One dog per person is allowed, always on a non-retractable lead; visitors must use the designated paths and respect restricted areas. The park has drinking fountains, waste-bag dispensers and places where dogs can wait while owners visit areas that do not admit pets. Its lush gardens and lakes make it a memorable outing with your dog in Sintra.

289.description: The Póvoa e Meadas reservoir near Castelo de Vide is a peaceful place to walk with your dog in the Alto Alentejo. The PR4 Barragem da Póvoa route is an easy, mostly flat trail of approximately 7.3 km, with views over the water, birdwatching spots and the Boa Morte necropolis.

290.description: Mila Intendente, on Avenida Almirante Reis in Lisbon, welcomes dogs of any size indoors and on the terrace, with no further restrictions specified. This all-day café serves brunch, lunch and speciality coffee, including its signature Crab Benedict alongside eggs, bowls and toast. It is a practical place to enjoy brunch with your dog in the Intendente area.

291.description: Mila Santos, on Rua Santos-o-Velho in Lisbon, welcomes dogs of any size indoors and on the terrace, with no additional restrictions specified. Known for all-day brunch, it serves avocado toast, eggs Benedict, pancakes, bowls, vegetarian and gluten-free options, speciality coffee and cocktails. A relaxed choice for eating with your dog in the historic Santos neighbourhood near the river.

292.description: Mugs Brunch Coffee, by Magoito Beach in the Sintra area, welcomes dogs of any size indoors and on its terrace, with no further restrictions specified. The menu includes brunch, pancakes, eggs Benedict, bowls, burgers, toast, juices, smoothies and coffee. It is a convenient place for a meal with your dog before or after a walk along the coast near Magoito.

293.description: Mabel’s Lisbon, near Avenida de Roma in the Alvalade area of Lisbon, welcomes dogs of any size indoors and on the terrace, with no additional restrictions specified. The small café specialises in thick, generously filled cookies, with flavours ranging from chocolate chips and pistachio to seasonal creations, as well as coffee and other drinks. It is an inviting stop for a freshly baked treat with your dog.

294.description: Grão Café & Bar, in Infantado, Loures, welcomes dogs indoors and outside. Larger dogs are discouraged from sitting indoors because the space is small. In a quiet, landscaped area, the café serves breakfast, brunch and casual meals, including bagels, toast, pancakes, burgers, salads and fresh juices. It is a pleasant spot for coffee or lunch with your dog in Loures.

295.description: Chão da Horta Country House in Papízios, Carregal do Sal, welcomes up to four dogs of any size. Dogs may stay indoors using their own beds, but cannot climb onto beds, sofas or armchairs. They are allowed in the swimming pool, and a washroom is available for bathing them. The property is fully walled and fenced. An extra €50 cleaning charge applies.

296.description: Legumi Sushi Vegan, on Rua Vicente Borga in Lisbon’s Madragoa neighbourhood, welcomes dogs of any size indoors and on the terrace, with no additional restrictions specified by the restaurant. Specialising in entirely vegan sushi, it replaces fish with creative combinations of vegetables, mushrooms, tofu, seaweed and other plant-based ingredients. A distinctive choice for Japanese-inspired food with your dog in Lisbon.

297.description: Fauna & Flora Estoril, on Rua Sacadura Cabral in Estoril, welcomes dogs of any size indoors and on the terrace. The café serves brunch and healthy food, including breakfast dishes, light meals, bowls, pancakes, juices and coffee. Its location makes it a convenient place to stop with your dog before or after a walk along the Cascais coast.

298.description: Zénite Rooftop Bar at Kimpton Atlântico Algarve in Albufeira welcomes dogs indoors and on the terrace, provided they stay on a lead. Water is available for pets. With panoramic Atlantic views, the rooftop offers signature cocktails, music and Peruvian- and Nikkei-inspired food, making it especially appealing in the late afternoon and at sunset. It is a relaxed place for a drink or light bite with your dog near the sea in Albufeira.

299.description: NAU São Rafael Suites in Albufeira is a five-star dog-friendly hotel accepting pets weighing up to 15 kg, with a maximum of one pet per room. Dogs may stay in family rooms and access permitted hotel areas but must be kept on a lead. There is an extra charge of €25 per night and a €100 deposit is required at check-in. The hotel provides a bed, bowl, water and a small surprise for your pet. With spacious outdoor areas and a location near São Rafael Beach, it is a comfortable option for an Algarve holiday with your dog.

300.description: Tascaria São Rafael in Albufeira is a dog-friendly restaurant at NAU São Rafael Suites, where dogs are welcome indoors. They must remain on a lead, and water is available for them. The restaurant is also open to guests who are not staying at the hotel and serves traditional Portuguese cuisine featuring local produce and regional flavours. It is a pleasant option for dinner with your dog in Albufeira, in a smart setting near São Rafael and Sesmarias beaches.

301.description: Kimpton Atlântico Algarve in Albufeira is a dog-friendly hotel welcoming dogs of any size or breed, with no limit on the number of pets and no additional fee or deposit. Pets may stay in rooms and access communal areas, terraces and outdoor spaces; the Wellness Hub Atlântico is the only restricted area. On request, the hotel provides a pet bed, food and water bowls, treats, toys and waste bags. It is a particularly flexible choice for staying with dogs in the Algarve without size restrictions or extra pet charges.

302.description: Pizzaria Luzzo Expo, on Alameda dos Oceanos in Parque das Nações, Lisbon, welcomes dogs on its terrace. The restaurant blends Italian tradition with Portuguese influences, serving slow-fermented sourdough pizzas, antipasti, calzones, salads, pasta and cocktails. It is a handy choice for an outdoor meal with your dog during a walk along the Tagus or through Parque das Nações.

303.description: Altentica Pizzaria in Ferreiras, Albufeira, welcomes dogs on its terrace, where water is available for pets. Dogs must remain on a lead. The restaurant specialises in freshly made pizza and pasta, with vegetarian and gluten-free options too. Its informal, family-friendly outdoor seating makes it a convenient choice for dinner with your dog in the Ferreiras area.

304.description: Palácio do Governador, a historic hotel in Belém, Lisbon, welcomes dogs and cats up to 10 kg, with a maximum of one pet per room. A €25 fee per pet per night applies. The hotel provides a pet kit with a bed, bowls, a snack and a door sign. Dogs may stay in the room and accompany owners in permitted outdoor areas, on a lead, with water available. Its location near Belém Tower makes it an appealing base for visiting Lisbon with a smaller pet.

305.description: The Westin Salgados Beach Resort in Albufeira welcomes dogs and cats weighing up to 10 kg, with a maximum of one pet per room. There is an additional charge of €17 per night. Pets may stay in the room, have water available and must be kept on a lead in permitted areas. Located between Salgados Beach and the lagoon in the Salgados Nature Reserve, the resort offers extensive outdoor spaces, pools, a spa and several restaurants for an Algarve holiday with your pet.

306.description: Praia de Paramos in Espinho allows dogs in the unpatrolled section of the beach. The broad Atlantic sands offer space for seaside walks, but visitors should respect the boundary between patrolled and unpatrolled areas, especially during the bathing season.

307.description: Nosolo Itália in Portimão, on Praça Manuel Teixeira Gomes, allows dogs on the terrace, so you can enjoy a meal together in the city centre. This is where the Nosolo Italia concept began, and the extensive Italian-inspired menu includes pizza, pasta, salads, meat, fish, crêpes, waffles and its well-known handmade ice cream. It's a practical place for lunch, dinner or an ice cream with your dog near Portimão's waterfront.

308.description: Pizzaria Casino da Ursa in Zambujeira do Mar welcomes dogs indoors and on its enclosed terrace, provided they stay on a lead. The restaurant serves wood-fired pizza, Portuguese dishes, meat, fresh fish, salads and vegetarian options on the Costa Vicentina.

309.description: Kuala Brunch Restaurant on Avenida Combatentes da Grande Guerra in Leiria welcomes dogs indoors and offers water. The tropical-inspired café serves all-day brunch, pancakes, bowls, filled croissants, wraps, vegetarian and vegan options, juices and smoothies.

310.description: TJELA – Restelo, on Rua Duarte Pacheco Pereira in Lisbon, welcomes dogs of any size indoors and outside, but only one dog at a time is permitted. The all-day menu includes its signature 'tjelas', pancakes, açaí, salads, burgers, vegetarian dishes and smoothies. It is a relaxed place to eat with your dog in Restelo, with both indoor and outdoor seating.

311.description: Croissants do Passarinho, on Avenida Dom José I in Amadora, welcomes dogs of all sizes indoors and on its terrace. Specialising in sweet and savoury croissants, it serves classic flavours and indulgent combinations such as Nutella and strawberries, salted caramel, pistachio, egg cream and almond, and Lotus Biscoff. It is a friendly stop for breakfast or an afternoon snack with your dog in Amadora.

312.description: Casas da Ribeira in Póvoa Velha, Seia, welcomes dogs and cats of all sizes indoors and outdoors. A €5 cleaning supplement applies to dogs weighing over 50 kg. Set in restored traditional granite houses in Serra da Estrela, the units have kitchens or kitchenettes and offer access to mountain walks.

313.description: Casa do Vinho Sintra Guest House, in Sintra’s historic centre, accepts pets on request for an indicated fee of €20 per accommodation unit per night. Food and water bowls are available in the room. The guest house has nine rooms, a garden and a terrace and is within walking distance of the National Palace and Quinta da Regaleira. Confirm pet conditions and availability before travelling.

314.description: Quinta das Murtas B&B in Sintra accepts one pet of any size in selected rooms for a supplement of €10 per night. Pets cannot enter the main house, where reception, lounges and breakfast facilities are located, but may stay in the designated accommodation, with food and water bowls provided. Surrounded by gardens, it is a peaceful base for exploring Sintra with your dog.

315.description: ibis Lisboa Sintra, in Mem Martins near Sintra, allows pets to stay in guest rooms for an additional fee. The hotel offers modern rooms, a bar, 24-hour snacks, private parking and convenient access to Sintra’s historic centre and hills. Confirm the pet charge, allowed size and number of animals before booking.

316.description: Castelo dos Mouros, the Moorish Castle in the Sintra hills, allows dogs with microchips, with one dog per visitor and a maximum of five dogs at the same time. Dogs must stay on a non-retractable lead, remain on designated paths and avoid restricted areas. A free dog ticket must be requested at the entrance. Additional muzzle, lead, handler and licence rules apply to breeds legally classified as potentially dangerous.

317.description: Moinho Dom Quixote, in Azóia near Cabo da Roca, welcomes dogs of all sizes, provided they remain on a lead. This bar and restaurant beside an old windmill has a large terrace overlooking the coast and serves brunch, sharing dishes, daily specials, and vegetarian and vegan options. It is a scenic place to relax with your dog after exploring Cabo da Roca.

318.description: Solar do Magoito, in São João das Lampas near Sintra, accepts pets when guests notify the property in advance and also has kennels on site. Set in a former manor house in the Sintra-Cascais Natural Park, it offers a garden, outdoor pool and rural surroundings near Magoito Beach. Confirm where your dog may stay and whether any charges apply before booking.

319.description: Pestana Sintra Golf, at Quinta da Beloura near Sintra, accepts dogs and cats weighing up to 15 kg in selected room categories for an extra charge. The hotel offers indoor and outdoor pools, a spa, gardens and access to the Beloura golf course. Tell the hotel you are bringing a pet before booking and confirm the applicable fee and room availability.

320.description: Penha Longa Resort in Linhó, near Sintra, accepts pets weighing up to 25 kg in selected accommodation, including certain Garden Wing suites and apartments, for an additional fee. Surrounded by the Sintra hills, the resort offers gardens, walking paths, golf, a spa and restaurants. Pet access depends on room type and availability, so mention your dog when booking and confirm the current fee and permitted areas.

321.description: Quinta de São Tadeu in Galamares, near Sintra, accepts pets on request, with an indicated supplement of €10 per pet per night, subject to the chosen room’s conditions. Set in a restored 250-year-old manor house with gardens and a terrace, it offers a peaceful place to stay with your dog near Monserrate and Sintra’s historic centre. Confirm availability and pet arrangements before booking.

322.description: NH Sintra Centro, close to Sintra’s historic centre, welcomes dogs and cats, up to a maximum of two animals per room. A fee of €25 per pet per night applies, and guests must contact the hotel before arrival and present a valid vaccination record at check-in. Guide dogs are exempt from the fee. Its central location makes it a practical base for visiting Sintra with your dog.

323.description: Pousada de Valença within the historic fortress welcomes dogs in guest rooms and communal areas, except the restaurant, always on a lead. The fee is €20 per pet per night, and the dog must be declared when booking. The property overlooks the Minho River and Tui.

324.description: Encosta do Monte in Arcozelo, near Ponte de Lima, welcomes dogs of any size without an additional fee under its published policy. The accommodation has a garden and parking, with easy access to the town and walks beside the Lima River. Confirm before booking.

325.description: Margarida da Praça in the historic centre of Viana do Castelo welcomes dogs on request without an extra charge. Its location close to the waterfront and Gil Eannes museum ship is handy for walks through the old town and beside the river.

326.description: Casa Azul d'Altamira in historic Viana do Castelo welcomes dogs on request, without an additional charge. The house has a garden, terrace, outdoor dining area and equipped kitchen, close to the river and Santa Luzia hill.

327.description: Quinta de Santo António in Sá, between Monção and Melgaço, welcomes dogs of any size for an indicated €10 per pet per night. Food and water bowls are available. The rural estate has gardens and a pool and is a peaceful base for exploring the Alvarinho wine region.

328.description: Casa Boavista in Formariz, Paredes de Coura, offers independent countryside chalets and welcomes dogs of any size without an extra fee under its published policy. Units have their own entrance and kitchen, with outdoor space and nature walks nearby. Confirm before booking.

329.description: Quinta Lamosa Ecoturismo in Gondoriz, Arcos de Valdevez, offers independent holiday houses near Peneda-Gerês National Park. Dogs are accepted on request, subject to accommodation conditions. Confirm availability, any fee and the rules before booking.

330.description: Hotel Cotto do Gatto in Grovelas, Ponte da Barca, welcomes dogs of any size without an additional charge. Pet beds and food and water bowls are provided. Its outdoor spaces and setting between the hills and Lima valley are convenient for exploring the area with your dog.

331.description: Casa dos Confrades on Praça Municipal in central Arcos de Valdevez accepts dogs on request, and additional charges may apply. The property has a garden, a seasonal outdoor pool and some units with kitchenettes, close to riverside walks along the Vez.

332.description: B&B HOTEL Viana do Castelo accepts dogs and cats for an indicated fee of €20 per pet per night. With a 24-hour reception and a location close to the centre, it provides a practical base for exploring Viana do Castelo with your dog. Confirm conditions and availability before booking.

333.description: Pousada Mosteiro de Amares in Bouro welcomes dogs weighing up to 15 kg in selected room types, subject to availability and an additional fee. Set in a restored 12th-century Cistercian monastery between Braga and Gerês, it requires advance confirmation of the room, pet supplement and permitted areas.

334.description: Mercure Braga Centro on Praceta João XXI accepts small dogs for an additional fee. The hotel has air-conditioned rooms, paid parking, an outdoor pool and a panoramic bar, but pet admission does not guarantee access to all facilities. Confirm the size limit, fee and permitted areas before booking.

335.description: ibis budget Braga Centro on Avenida da Liberdade accepts dogs for an additional fee. Close to Forum Braga and the historic centre, it provides simple air-conditioned rooms with private bathrooms. Confirm the pet fee, size restrictions and permitted areas before reserving.

336.description: Holiday Inn Braga welcomes dogs and cats weighing up to 15 kg for a published €35 nightly supplement. A pet bed, bowl and walking area are provided. Pets cannot enter the restaurant or pool area, and the terrace is also off limits in summer. Declare your pet when booking.

337.description: ibis Guimarães Centro in Creixomil welcomes dogs for an additional fee. Local tourism information states a maximum of one pet per room and recommends carrying the dog's legal documents. Confirm the current fee, permitted size and access to communal areas before booking.

338.description: INNSiDE Braga Centro on Avenida Central accepts one pet weighing up to 15 kg, subject to availability. The published supplement is €35 per night. Mention your pet when booking and confirm which common areas are accessible.

339.description: B&B HOTEL Guimarães on Rua Rómulo de Carvalho accepts dogs for an additional fee to be confirmed at booking. Around a 15-minute walk from the castle, it offers air-conditioned rooms and a 24-hour reception. Keep dogs on a lead, carry them or use a carrier, and follow staff guidance in the breakfast area. Confirm the size limit with the hotel.

340.description: Pousada Mosteiro de Guimarães in Costa accepts one dog weighing up to 15 kg per room, subject to availability and an additional fee. Dogs must stay accompanied and on a lead and cannot enter dining areas, bars or social spaces. Bring the required documents and confirm the current supplement before booking.

341.description: Meliá Braga Hotel & Spa welcomes up to two pets per Standard room, subject to availability, each weighing no more than 20 kg. The supplement is €35 per pet per night, and a €100 deposit may be requested. Pet admission to rooms does not imply access to the spa or pools; confirm permitted areas with the hotel.

342.description: ibis Braga Centro on Rua do Carmo welcomes small dogs for an additional fee. Close to the municipal market and historic centre, the hotel has air-conditioned rooms, Wi-Fi and a 24-hour bar and snack service. Confirm the weight limit, pet fee and rules for shared areas when booking.

343.description: Chaxoila – Casa de Pasto in Borralha, near the EN2 outside Vila Real, is a restaurant dedicated to northern Portuguese regional cooking and local produce. Specific dog-access rules have not been recorded; check with the restaurant before visiting.

344.description: Adega da Luz in Chaves describes itself as pet-friendly and serves Spanish-inspired tapas and small plates. It is an option for eating with your dog while visiting the city.

345.description: AquaBarroso campsite by the Alto Rabagão reservoir in Penedones accepts dogs on leads. Open from April to October, it has pitches for tents, caravans and motorhomes in a mountain setting. Check any additional pet charges when booking. Acceptance at the campsite does not automatically include access to its restaurant or water activities.

346.description: Pedras Salgadas Spa & Nature Park in Vila Pouca de Aguiar is a pet-friendly eco-resort set in a wooded thermal park. Confirm the eligible accommodation type, size limit and pet supplement directly before booking. Dog access to the spa, pools and restaurant has not been confirmed.

347.description: Nosso Shopping in Vila Real allows registered dogs in designated common areas and participating shops. Pre-register in the app and have the required documents checked at the information desk. Dogs must be accompanied, and the issued tag should remain visible. The food court and children's play area are excluded; follow signs for toilets and lifts.

348.description: Hotel Rural Misarela in Sidros, Montalegre, accepts dogs and offers a base for exploring the Barroso mountains near the Misarela Bridge and Salamonde reservoir. Tell the hotel your dog's size and confirm the current fee and permitted areas when booking.

349.description: Vidago Palace in the Vidago thermal park welcomes one dog weighing up to 20 kg, or one cat, per room in Garden and Garden Deluxe room types only. The published supplement is €60 per night. Pets are not allowed in the hotel's public areas. Confirm availability and conditions before booking.

350.description: Taberna S. Tiago in Fafião, Montalegre, welcomes well-behaved dogs indoors and outdoors. The indoor dining room is small, so admission may be limited if other dogs are already present. The tavern serves regional Portuguese food, including cured meats, cheese, cod, octopus and meat dishes, in a Gerês mountain village setting.

351.description: Parque Canino de Lordelo near Feira do Levante in Vila Real provides a dedicated area for dogs to exercise and socialise. Check the posted rules on arrival, supervise your dog and consider how it interacts with other dogs.

352.description: Magnífico Douro welcomes dogs on its traditional rabelo boat trips departing from Pinhão. Dogs must remain under their owners' supervision during the cruise. Mention your dog when booking and confirm the conditions for the trip you choose.

353.description: Villa das Oliveiras between Comporta, Grândola and Melides may accept dogs subject to advance approval. Each request is assessed individually according to the number and type of dogs. The property has around three hectares of land but is not fully fenced. Contact the owners before booking to confirm whether your dogs can stay.

354.description: Pavilhão do Conhecimento – Ciência Viva, in Parque das Nações, Lisbon, welcomes pets throughout the year under specific entry rules. Before visiting, register at the ticket office with the owner’s identification, an up-to-date pet health record or passport and proof of microchipping. A free PATAporte is then issued, valid for one year. Dogs must use a non-retractable lead of no more than one metre and a muzzle where legally required. They may enter the foyer, exhibitions and common areas, but not the café interior or Casa Inacabada. Limits are two pets per person and four per group; water and waste bags are available outside.

355.description: Sierra Melides Villa in Melides welcomes dogs of any size indoors, although they must not go on beds or sofas. No maximum number is specified, but prior confirmation is required. There is no extra pet fee. The accommodation includes houses with private pools in a natural setting near the Melides and Comporta beaches.

356.description: Café Kapheina in São Bartolomeu de Messines, in the municipality of Silves, welcomes dogs on the terrace and provides water for them. Located in the centre of the village, it is a handy place to stop for coffee, breakfast or a light meal with your dog at an outdoor table. The terrace and available water make visits more comfortable, whether you're walking around Messines or stopping on a journey through inland Algarve.

357.description: The Therapist Alvalade, on Rua José d’Esaguy in Lisbon, welcomes dogs on its outdoor terrace and provides water for them. The restaurant focuses on natural, mindful eating, with mainly vegetarian and vegan dishes alongside some fish options, using seasonal and local ingredients where possible. It is an attractive spot for breakfast, lunch or a light meal with your dog in Alvalade.

358.description: Gal Café, in the Anjos neighbourhood of Lisbon, is a vegan café welcoming dogs indoors and providing water for them. Its entirely plant-based menu includes breakfast, brunch, pancakes, croissants, sandwiches, bowls, cakes, smoothies and speciality coffee, with some Brazilian influences. Food, music and small art exhibitions create an informal neighbourhood atmosphere where you can relax with your dog inside.

359.description: A Minha Avó, on Avenida António Augusto de Aguiar in Lisbon, is a vegan restaurant welcoming dogs indoors, with water available for them. Its plant-based menu reimagines traditional Portuguese favourites such as bitoque, cod with cream, francesinha, duck-style rice and bifana, alongside homemade desserts. It is a comfortable place to explore vegan Portuguese cooking with your dog.

360.description: Inquieta, in Campolide, Lisbon, is an independent bookshop and café welcoming dogs indoors. Spread over two floors, it combines books from independent publishers with an entirely plant-based café serving toast, quiche, cakes, cookies, coffee and tea. It is a quiet, welcoming place to read or take a break with your dog in Lisbon.

361.description: Green Bunny Coffee & Juice in Charneca de Caparica welcomes dogs indoors and on its terrace, with water available. The all-day brunch menu features eggs Benedict, pancakes, salads, bowls, croissants, fresh juices and coffee.

362.description: A Lanchonete in Belém, on Rua Pinto Ferreira in Lisbon, welcomes dogs of any size indoors and on the terrace, with biscuits for pets. The family-rooted, Brazilian-inspired menu includes brunch, pão de queijo, tapioca, açaí, burgers and savoury pastries. It is a relaxed stop for a meal with your dog, within reach of walks along the Tagus River.

363.description: A Lanchonete (Benfica), listed in Lisbon, welcomes dogs of any size indoors and on its terrace and offers them biscuits. The Brazilian-inspired menu includes brunch, pão de queijo, tapioca, açaí, burgers and savoury pastries. The original listing contains conflicting location details, so confirm the exact branch and address before visiting with your dog.

364.description: Almada Forum shopping centre allows dogs and cats on leads in its common areas. Pets cannot enter the food court or hypermarket, and individual shops decide whether to allow them inside. Check the signs at each entrance.

365.description: A Lanchonete Parede, on Avenida da República in Parede, welcomes dogs of any size indoors and on its terrace, with biscuits for four-legged visitors. Its Brazilian-inspired menu includes pão de queijo, coxinhas, fried pastries, burgers, brunch and feijoada on selected days. Located in Parede’s traditional shopping area on the Cascais railway line, it is an inviting stop with your dog throughout the year.

366.description: Atelier d’A Lanchonete, on Avenida da Ilha da Madeira in Restelo, Lisbon, welcomes dogs of any size indoors and on the terrace, with biscuits available for pets. Part café and part creative workshop for the brand, it serves Brazilian favourites such as pão de queijo, savoury pastries and açaí, alongside cakes, brunch and coffee roasted on site. The small space has seating indoors and outside.

367.description: Farmácia Penha de França, on Avenida Coronel Eduardo Galhardo in Lisbon, welcomes dogs indoors and provides water for them. Alongside dispensing medicines, the pharmacy offers health services such as nutrition and podiatry appointments, vaccinations, basic health checks and pharmaceutical advice. Its extended opening hours make it a convenient place to run essential errands with your dog in Penha de França.

368.description: Brant Parque das Nações, on Rua Cais das Naus in Lisbon, welcomes dogs both indoors and on the terrace and provides water for them. Open throughout the day, it serves breakfast and brunch dishes such as sandwiches, wraps, eggs, croissants, bowls and coffee drinks. The nearby Tagus waterfront and walking paths make it easy to combine a meal or coffee break with a stroll with your dog.

369.description: Good Company Books, in Avenidas Novas, Lisbon, is a bookshop and café welcoming dogs indoors. Specialising in English-language books, it offers international literature and translated Portuguese-language works in a space designed for reading, working or meeting friends. The café serves locally roasted speciality coffee, pastries and small bites, while Portuguese wine by the glass is available later in the day. A distinctive dog-friendly stop for book lovers in Lisbon.

370.description: Parque Canino de Sacavém, in the Quinta do Património development in Sacavém, is a fenced dog park of approximately 400 m² where dogs can exercise and play off-lead. The enclosure has training equipment, a drinking fountain, benches and waste bins. Created by the local parish authorities, it provides a dedicated place for dog exercise and socialisation near Lisbon.

371.description: As Marias Brunch & Coffee on Rua Conselheiro Albuquerque in Castelo Branco welcomes dogs indoors. The relaxed café serves eggs Benedict, pancakes, waffles, toast, brownies and other breakfast and brunch options alongside coffee and drinks.

372.description: Meliá Castelo Branco welcomes pets in guest rooms subject to availability. Up to two pets per room are allowed, with a combined weight of no more than 15 kg. The fee is €35 per pet per night, and a €100 deposit may be requested at check-in. The hotel offers a pet kit with a blanket, food and water bowls, water and a biscuit. Confirm access to other hotel facilities.

373.description: Parque do Barrocal in Castelo Branco is a natural area of around 40 hectares where dogs may accompany visitors on a lead at all times. Part of the UNESCO Naturtejo Global Geopark, it has trails, boardwalks, seven viewpoints, granite formations, a birdwatching area and a suspension bridge. Dogs must not be let off lead.

374.description: Forum Castelo Branco shopping centre permits dogs only when carried in a suitable pet carrier or, for small dogs, held in their owner's arms. Dogs may not walk through the centre on a lead.

375.description: Passadiço da Duna da Cresmina is a community-suggested place in Cascais. Detailed dog-access conditions have not yet been recorded, so check the local signage before visiting with your dog.

376.description: Mundi Food Café in Almada welcomes dogs indoors and on its terrace and provides water. The all-day menu includes pancakes, eggs Benedict, bowls, burgers, tapioca dishes, salads, smoothies and vegetarian and vegan options.

377.description: Faz Frio, in Príncipe Real, Lisbon, allows dogs indoors, although the restaurant is small and does not prominently advertise its pet policy. With more than a century of history, it specialises in traditional Portuguese cooking, including bacalhau à Zé do Pipo, cod fritters, alheira croquettes, fried green beans and pica-pau. It is an atmospheric option for a meal with your dog in central Lisbon; checking ahead may be helpful given the limited space.

378.description: Santa Clara dos Cogumelos, on the upper floor of Mercado de Santa Clara in Lisbon, welcomes dogs. Close to the Feira da Ladra flea market, the restaurant specialises in dishes built around mushrooms, from starters to desserts, including wild and cultivated varieties, risotto, small plates and vegetarian options. With an informal setting and views towards the Tagus, it offers an unusual dining stop with your dog while exploring São Vicente and Alfama.

379.description: Tryga Pizzaria e Gelataria – Baía do Seixal on Rua Paiva Coelho welcomes dogs indoors and on its terrace, with water available. The restaurant serves artisan pizzas, pasta, burrata, salads and Italian desserts. Its position near Seixal Bay makes it easy to combine a meal with a waterside walk.

380.description: Pizzaria Massa Fina in Lourinhã welcomes dogs both indoors and on its terrace. The owners make an effort to accommodate visitors with dogs, including adjusting seating or arranging an outdoor table when possible. Known for its thin-crust pizzas, the small, family-run restaurant offers a variety of toppings and vegetarian options. It is a friendly choice for a relaxed meal with your dog in Lourinhã.

381.description: Taverna Antiqua in Tomar welcomes dogs indoors. This medieval-themed restaurant combines period-inspired food with themed décor, live music and entertainment during banquets. Its Portuguese and Mediterranean-inspired menu includes vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free choices.

382.description: Mundi Green in Almada welcomes dogs indoors and outdoors and provides water. The relaxed café serves brunch, bowls, salads, burgers, pancakes and vegetarian and vegan dishes, with a terrace for eating with your dog.

383.description: EPOCA – Osteria Italiana, in Parque das Nações, Lisbon, welcomes dogs indoors and on its terrace, with water available for pets. Close to the Tagus River and Vasco da Gama Tower, the restaurant serves traditional Italian family recipes, fresh pasta, homemade desserts and Italian wines. The nearby riverside promenade makes it easy to combine a meal with a walk with your dog.

384.description: Tosca Melides on the EN261-2 in Melides welcomes dogs of any size both indoors and on its terrace. This relaxed Italian-inspired pizzeria serves pizzas, pasta, salads and vegetarian options, making it easy to dine with your dog.

385.description: Estrela Serenity Resort in Folgosinho, Gouveia, accepts dogs subject to prior approval, availability and an additional fee. Some guest rooms have a private outdoor area for pets. Dogs must be kept on a lead and cannot enter the restaurant interior, pool area or other marked restricted zones. Water is available for dogs. The resort offers a nature-focused stay in Serra da Estrela.

386.description: Kong – Food Made With Compassion, on Rua do Corpo Santo in Lisbon’s Cais do Sodré area, welcomes dogs of any size indoors and often has biscuits for four-legged visitors. There is no terrace. The entirely plant-based menu offers vegan versions of Portuguese favourites, including bitoque, francesinha, cod-style fritters, fried cuttlefish-style dishes and feijoada, as well as house-made desserts. Its animal-friendly philosophy makes it a particularly fitting stop with your dog in Lisbon.

387.description: Restaurante O Castiço in Mealhada welcomes dogs indoors. Founded in 1975, this family restaurant specialises in Portuguese and Bairrada cuisine, including roast suckling pig, chanfana, cod and octopus. An indoor dining option for visitors exploring Mealhada with their dogs.

388.description: Palácio da Lousã Boutique Hotel in Lousã welcomes dogs and cats weighing up to 25 kg. Pets may stay in guest rooms and accompany owners in the restaurant and bar, but must remain accompanied and on a lead in shared areas. The spa and outdoor pool are off limits. Pet registration and a charge of €40 per animal per night apply, and a small welcome kit is provided.

389.description: Pão do Rogil, in Rogil in the municipality of Aljezur, welcomes dogs on its terraces. This artisan bakery on the Vicentine Coast makes bread, cakes and biscuits inspired by regional flavours, including Aljezur sweet potatoes, carob and almonds. The menu also includes toasties, sandwiches, pies, focaccia, savoury croissants and ice cream. Its several outdoor terraces make it a convenient place to stop with your dog while exploring the Vicentine Coast.

390.description: MÁDÁ in Sítio de Santa Susana, Aljezur, is a dog-friendly restaurant that welcomes dogs indoors and on the terrace, with water available for them. The steakhouse and bar focuses on cuts of meat and relaxed meals made for sharing. The restaurant confirms that pets are welcome as long as its rules and other guests' comfort are respected. Its position beside the EN120 makes it a convenient stop when travelling through Aljezur with your dog.

391.description: Balagan Ericeira, at Praia do Sul in Ericeira, welcomes dogs indoors and on its terrace. Its Mediterranean cuisine draws strongly on Middle Eastern flavours, seasonal ingredients and vegan and gluten-free options. The venue includes a café and deli downstairs and a rooftop restaurant overlooking the Atlantic, serving breakfast, lunch, dinner and cocktails. It is a relaxed, sea-view restaurant for dining with your dog in Ericeira.

392.description: Cais do Parque in Caldas da Rainha welcomes dogs on its terrace and provides water. Set beside the lake in Parque D. Carlos I, this restaurant and cocktail bar serves meat, fish, vegetarian dishes and internationally inspired food. The park setting makes it easy to combine a meal with a walk.

393.description: The Cascais seafront promenade, known as the Paredão de Cascais, is an approximately three-kilometre coastal walking route between Cascais and São João do Estoril. Dogs may accompany walkers when properly registered and kept on a lead, with a muzzle where legally required. Owners must clean up after their pets. Beaches, cafés and sea views along the way make it a popular place for a walk with your dog on the Cascais and Estoril coast.

394.description: Palácio Baldaya in Benfica, Lisbon, welcomes dogs on the café terrace and in the outdoor garden. Housed in a restored palace, this cultural venue brings together a library, children’s play area, coworking spaces, exhibitions and events, as well as a café with a leafy outdoor area. It is a relaxing place to take a break with your dog in Benfica while enjoying the garden or cultural surroundings.

395.description: Fração D'Ouro in Sesimbra accepts small dogs that are accustomed to living indoors, with no stated limit on their number. Dogs may stay throughout the accommodation, and a fee of €10 per pet per night applies. There is no outdoor space, but Praia da Califórnia and Sesimbra's historic centre are a short walk away.

396.description: Mahalo Restaurant & Bar in Santa Bárbara de Nexe, in the municipality of Faro, welcomes dogs both indoors and on the terrace. The relaxed restaurant combines Portuguese and Mediterranean food, with meat, fish, small plates, vegan options and cocktails. It has outdoor tables and a rooftop bar, and the restaurant explicitly allows pets. If you're looking for somewhere to eat with your dog in inland Algarve, you can choose indoor or outdoor seating.

397.description: Restaurante O Ténis in Portimão welcomes dogs on its terrace, which sits in a fenced outdoor area. Located beside the Municipal Tennis Complex, the restaurant serves traditional Algarve cuisine, including fresh fish, tapas-style dishes and charcoal-grilled specialities such as grilled sardines and cuttlefish. Its spacious terrace is a practical option for enjoying a meal outdoors with your dog in Portimão.

398.description: wecamp Reserva Alecrim in Ademas, Santiago do Cacém, is a dog-friendly glamping retreat with selected accommodation types that accept pets. Some offer pet kits on request. Not all units allow dogs, so check when booking. Between Santiago do Cacém and Melides, the retreat combines domes, villas and bungalows with outdoor areas and pools.

399.description: Honest Greens Chiado, on Rua Ivens in central Lisbon, accepts dogs, although it has not specified exactly which indoor or outdoor areas they may use. Near Praça Luís de Camões, the restaurant focuses on healthy food with seasonal ingredients, customisable dishes and vegetarian, vegan and keto choices. Contact the restaurant before visiting to confirm where your dog may stay.

400.description: Pastelaria Colibri II in Galé, Albufeira, welcomes dogs on its terrace, which has plenty of shade and water available for pets. Known for pastries, coffee, breakfast and light meals, it has several outdoor tables where you can take a comfortable break with your dog. Located near Galé Shopping Centre, close to the beaches and main roads in this part of Albufeira, it is a practical stop for breakfast, brunch or coffee during a walk around Galé.

401.description: Alma e Tejo, in the riverside linear park of Póvoa de Santa Iria, welcomes dogs on its outdoor terrace and provides water for them. Dogs must remain on a lead. Its position beside the Tagus River and nearby walking paths makes it an inviting spot for a meal or drink before or after a riverside walk with your dog.

402.description: The Praia da Adraga–Praia Grande boardwalk in Colares, near Sintra, crosses the protected Adraga–Praia Grande Ecological Park and offers a scenic walk with your dog between the hills and the Atlantic. Wooden boardwalks and marked paths pass through restored habitats, viewpoints and areas of geological and archaeological interest, with views of both beaches. To protect this sensitive landscape, keep your dog close and stay on the designated routes.

403.description: Casa dos Torricados in Santarém welcomes dogs in its fenced outdoor dining area, where water is available and dogs must stay on a lead. The restaurant specialises in traditional Ribatejo flavours, particularly torricado bread served with fish or meat.

404.description: Malte Taberna in Trofa welcomes dogs indoors and on its terrace, provided they remain on a lead. The informal tavern serves snacks, burgers, sandwiches and craft beer, offering a relaxed meal with your dog.

411.description: Catramóia Praia in Lourinhã is dog-friendly holiday accommodation where dogs can stay indoors with their owners and water is available for pets. The apartment offers a practical base for travelling with your dog near the coast, with opportunities for walks and seaside outings around Lourinhã.

412.description: Catramóia Pet Friendly in Colmeal da Torre, Belmonte, welcomes dogs inside the holiday home. A fenced outdoor area gives dogs space to enjoy the property, and water is available. It is a convenient base for exploring the Belmonte area with your dog.

413.description: Aleixo's House in Santo Aleixo, Monforte, welcomes up to three dogs per stay, with no size restriction. Dogs may move throughout the house and outdoor areas, but must not go on beds or use the accommodation's blankets and towels. There is no pet fee, although a refundable €90 deposit is required and may be retained for damage or additional cleaning. Food and water bowls for small and medium dogs are available. The property also has a saltwater pool.

414.description: Casa do Trapo in Mivaqueiro, Sardoal, welcomes dogs without size or weight restrictions. Dogs may stay in the room and move around the fully fenced property. There is no extra pet fee, and a swimming pool is available for guests.

415.description: Casa do Mogadouro Eco-turismo in Mogadouro welcomes dogs in guest rooms, with no stated size or number limit. There is an additional €5 charge per animal. The accommodation has a fenced outdoor area and a swimming pool, surrounded by the countryside of Trás-os-Montes.

416.description: Monte do Carapetal in Amareleja, Moura, welcomes dogs of any size and number. They can move throughout the holiday home, and an additional €50 per stay applies. The property has a fenced outdoor space and swimming pool, offering a base for a break in the Alentejo with your dogs.

417.description: Atelier20th in Ervidel, Aljustrel, is a holiday home welcoming dogs of any size. The first two dogs stay without a supplement; a €30 fee applies from the third dog. Dogs can use the entire house and fenced garden. There is no pool, but nearby open countryside and the Roxo reservoir, about 2 km away, offer places to explore. Pet-sitting services and local dog-friendly restaurant suggestions are available on request.

418.description: Bloomoon House in Bunheiro, Murtosa, near the Ria de Aveiro, accepts up to two dogs per room and five across the property, with no size restriction. Dogs may stay in the room and use permitted areas of the property. The outdoor space has a wall and fence around 1.2 metres high. Dogs cannot enter the pool area, should be supervised around other pets and must not be left alone on the property.

419.description: Villas Safara in Safara, Moura, welcomes dogs of any size and has no stated limit on their number. Dogs may accompany guests throughout the accommodation. An extra fee of €50 per stay applies. The property has a fenced outdoor area and a swimming pool, making it an option for a dog-friendly break in the Alentejo.

420.description: Aldeia Museu José Franco, also known as Aldeia Típica José Franco, in Sobreiro near Mafra, welcomes dogs on a lead accompanied by their owners. This free-to-visit open-air village museum recreates traditional rural life in the Lisbon region through historic workshops, shops, windmills, miniature buildings, pottery and local crafts. It is a pleasant place to explore with your dog, and a bakery on site serves the region’s traditional chouriço bread.

421.description: Burger Queens in Costa da Caparica welcomes dogs indoors, where they should remain on a lead. Water is available for dogs. Close to Praia Nova and the seafront promenade, it is a convenient spot to eat after a walk by the sea.

422.description: Pena D’Água Boutique Hotel & Villas in Covilhã welcomes pets of any size, with up to three per room subject to confirmation. Pets may stay in the room and access the bar, reception and outdoor areas, including the poolside, but they cannot enter the pool. Bowls and pet beds are available on advance request. Pets are not allowed in the breakfast room, although alternatives are offered in the lounge bar or room. One pet is allowed in the Açafrão restaurant.

423.description: Vai… Vai Gerês, in the centre of Gerês village, welcomes dogs both indoors and on the terrace. Dogs must be kept on a lead throughout the visit. Being able to choose between indoor and outdoor seating makes it convenient at different times of year. It's a good place to stop for a drink, lunch or dinner before or after exploring the Gerês region with your dog.

424.description: Cantinho Redondo in Froufe, Ponte da Barca, is dog-friendly accommodation that accepts up to two dogs per stay, with no size restrictions or extra pet fee. The house is in Peneda-Gerês National Park, in a peaceful natural setting close to the river and small lagoons. It's a great base for exploring Gerês and enjoying outdoor walks and hikes with your dog.

425.description: Tanoa Café, in Lisbon’s Bairro Alto neighbourhood, welcomes dogs indoors regardless of size. There is no outdoor terrace, but dogs are welcome inside the café. The menu focuses on brunch, with eggs Benedict, pancakes, speciality coffee, matcha and other freshly prepared options. If you're looking for somewhere to stop with your dog in central Lisbon, it's a relaxed and welcoming choice.
